title: Why the Middle of a List Is Harder to Remember
description: An illustrated example of the serial-position effect in immediate free recall. This is a general research pattern, not a test of your memory.
fact_text: Which part of a list will you remember best? In immediate free recall, people often remember the first and last words better than the middle. This is the serial-position effect. Early words can get more rehearsal. The last words were heard most recently. These advantages are called primacy and recency. But the pattern can change with the task and the time before recall. So this isn't a trick that predicts your personal memory. It's a recurring pattern researchers see when they compare positions in a list.

sources.title: Serial position effects in free memory recall: An ERP study
sources.claim: Recall can be better for items near the beginning and end of a list than for items in between.
